::: {.why}
A pipeline that works when you run it by hand and a pipeline that works when it runs itself are different pipelines, and the difference shows up in the environment rather than in the code.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Diagnose the first unattended run entirely from its logs and monitors, without rerunning it.
- Fix whatever broke and say which category of failure it was.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Read the logs before touching anything: what ran, what each step took, what the monitors said, and what the reconciliation reported. Diagnosing from logs alone is the skill being tested, and if you cannot, the logging work from day 324 is incomplete rather than the run being at fault.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Fix what broke, which will be an environment difference: a path that resolved differently, a credential not in the scheduler's environment, a timezone assumption, or a dependency on a shell profile. Write which category it was into the runbook, because the next one will be from the same list.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The pipeline runs unattended on a schedule, and the first failure is diagnosed from logs alone and fixed, with the failure category recorded in the runbook.
:::
